cohort: 200 women with high BMI at first antenatal visit (BMI ≥ 30), and 203 women with normal BMI (BMI 18.5-29.9) who had delivered at SMC between 16 July 2016 till 15 July 2017
finding: Pregnant women with high BMI had significantly higher rates of recurrent pregnancy loss, gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, cesarean section delivery, instrumental delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, wound infection, stillbirth, neonatal death, macrosomia, low Apgar score, and congenital anomalies.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was significantly more common in women with high BMI (54.5%) as compared to women with normal BMI (34%) (p-value = 0.000).
